claims.statement: The tracked root .env.example is the single configuration source shared by the backend, the Huey worker, Docker Compose interpolation and the frontend service; docker-compose.yml loads it via env_file for backend and worker, interpolates ports/URLs from it, and forwards VITE_* values plus JWT_SECRET to the frontend service.

docker-compose.yml derives the frontend SSR guard secret from the root .env by mapping SECRET_KEY to JWT_SECRET with a required-variable assertion, so frontend/src/hooks.server.ts verifies the auth_token cookie with the same HS256 key the backend signs with and no separate secret is configured.

Settings.model_config pins env_file to the literal ".env" relative to the working directory and uses extra="ignore", so stray files such as src/.env are ignored and unknown keys are tolerated; process environment variables override file values and defaults apply when no file exists.

Settings validates SECRET_KEY in an after-model validator: outside dev/test environments the key must be non-empty and at least MIN_SECRET_KEY_LENGTH = 32 characters or Settings() raises a ValidationError; dev and test may leave it empty.
Settings applies a before-field validator to smtp_sender_email that substitutes noreply@retail-portfolio.local when the configured value is missing or blank.

settings is a module-level Settings() singleton instantiated at import time, and consumers read it as an object (call-time attribute access) rather than re-instantiating Settings, which is why tests monkeypatch attributes on the singleton.

register_services in src/config/services.py is the single registration entry point for both the API and the worker: it registers the AsyncSession factory from the passed DatabaseSessionManager, registers core, account and auth services unconditionally, and then selects stub or live integration and market registrations based on settings.stub_external_api.

When settings.stub_external_api is true, register_services calls register_integration_stub_services and register_market_stub_services instead of the live functions, and only two abstract keys get a different implementation: WealthsimpleApiGateway resolves to StubWealthsimpleApiGateway instead of wealthsimple_api_wrapper_factory, and AIService resolves to StubAIService instead of ai_service_factory; every other key in the stub path uses the same factory object as the live path, so callers resolve identical keys regardless of the branch.

src/market/eodhd.py::eodhd_gateway_factory independently re-checks settings.stub_external_api and returns StubEodhdGateway instead of EodhdGateway, so the live market registration path still yields a stub gateway when stub mode is on; the registry-level and factory-level switches must stay consistent.

A new repository, service or domain API is only resolvable if it is registered in its domain's register_*_services function; the API process attaches the resulting registry to app.state.svcs_registry and route handlers receive a request-scoped svcs.fastapi.DepContainer for aget calls.

The Huey worker builds a second, independent registry in its on_startup handler using a fresh DatabaseSessionManager configured with NullPool, and stores it on huey.svcs_registry; NullPool avoids operation-in-progress errors when pooled async connections are reused across the per-task asyncio.run() event loops.

Huey task bodies resolve services through async with Container(huey.svcs_registry) after guarding for a missing registry: critical periodic tasks in src/market/task.py and src/account/task.py raise RuntimeError("Worker registry not initialized") while best-effort tasks such as _generate_note_title and _check_and_dispatch_price_alerts return early.

Task modules must import src.worker.huey and be imported by src/worker.py for their tasks to register with Huey; tests assert registration by looking up the qualified task name in huey._registry._registry.

DatabaseSessionManager owns one AsyncEngine and an async_sessionmaker(autocommit=False, expire_on_commit=False); session() rolls back on exception and always closes the session, connect() rolls back the connection on exception, and both raise SystemError if the manager was never initialized or has been closed.

A module-level sessionmanager is created from settings.database_url and settings.echo_sql and is imported directly by the API process, while the worker constructs its own NullPool instance from the same URL.
Alembic migrations run automatically at API startup through run_migrations(), which calls alembic.command.upgrade to head inside asyncio.to_thread; the step is skipped when environment is "test".

migrations/env.py imports each domain's model module so every table is registered on BaseModel.metadata before target_metadata is captured, derives target_metadata from src.config.database.BaseModel, and overrides sqlalchemy.url from the DATABASE_URL environment variable by rewriting postgresql+asyncpg:// to synchronous postgresql:// for the NullPool sync engine.

RedisManager keeps one redis.asyncio client per running event loop in a dictionary guarded by a threading.Lock: client() prunes and closes clients whose loop has closed, then lazily creates a decode_responses=True client for the current loop, which lets the single redis_manager singleton serve the request loop, the WebSocket listener and asyncio.run() task loops; every client is also built with bounded DEFAULT_SOCKET_TIMEOUT and DEFAULT_SOCKET_CONNECT_TIMEOUT of 5.0 seconds so a stalled server fails fast, and close() clears the dictionary and closes the remaining clients.

The redis_manager singleton is constructed from settings.redis_url and is the shared Redis access point for the auth token denylist, TOTP/passkey challenges, account sync status, the market security search cache and WebSocket fan-out; IndicatorCache instead builds its own client from settings.redis_url with decode_responses=False.

Tests never depend on a real Redis server: the autouse fake_redis_manager fixture replaces the shared redis_manager singleton's client (and the redis_manager aliases imported by src.auth.api and src.auth.service) with an in-memory FakeRedis, and mock_redis_storage exposes the backing store for assertions.

The slowapi Limiter is module-level with headers_enabled=True, is attached as app.state.limiter with SlowAPIMiddleware and the rate-limit-exceeded handler, and uses memory:// storage when ENVIRONMENT or settings.environment is "test" and settings.redis_url otherwise; the limiter is constructed at import time, so it never sees later test monkeypatching of settings.

Rate limiting is keyed by user_or_ip_key_func, which decodes the auth_token cookie or Authorization header with settings.secret_key to return user:{user_id} from user_id or sub and otherwise falls back to the request's remote address, making the limit per authenticated user when a valid token is present.

Rate limits are applied per route with @limiter.limit decorators: 5/minute on POST /auth/signup, 10/minute on /auth/login, /auth/2fa/login-verify and both passkey-authenticate routes, 3/minute on POST /auth/resend-verification, POST /accounts/{account_id}/sync, POST /integration/accounts/import and POST /integration/positions/import, and 5/minute on each of the three AI endpoints under /securities/{security_id}/ai/*.

src/core/context.py exposes the request_id ContextVar through set_request_id (returning a reset token) and get_request_id, and Huey tasks reuse it by accepting a request_id argument, setting it, and resetting the token in a finally block so task logs inherit the originating request's correlation ID.

RequestIdMiddleware reuses an inbound X-Request-ID header or generates a UUID, stores it on request.state.request_id and the contextvar, logs one line per request with duration_ms at INFO or WARNING for 4xx, logs and re-raises on exception, echoes X-Request-ID on the response, and always resets the contextvar in a finally block.

init_logging() emits JSON logs via JsonFormatter and a RequestIdFilter when environment is "prod" (fields timestamp, level, logger, message, request_id plus optional user_id, domain, duration_ms, exc_info and stack_info), and otherwise uses a forced-terminal rich Console with a FallbackRichHandler that degrades to a stderr stream handler.

init_logging() calls logging.basicConfig(force=True), clears handlers on every existing logger and sets propagate=True so third-party loggers route through the root handler, quiets urllib3/httpx/watchfiles/faker/svcs/redis to INFO, and disables uvicorn.access because RequestIdMiddleware already logs each request.
Log level resolution in init_logging() prefers settings.log_level, then WARNING when environment is "test", then DEBUG.

settings.environment is the runtime mode switch consulted across the codebase: it enables debugpy in dev, sets FastAPI debug, adds a permissive origin regex and error-detail redaction outside prod, sets secure/httponly cookie flags in prod, selects MemoryHuey versus RedisHuey in test, and skips startup migrations in test.

The /health/ready endpoint resolves an AsyncSession from the svcs container, executes select(1), pings Redis through redis_manager.client(), and returns 200 when both report ok or 503 with status "degraded" otherwise.
The market document upload route reads settings.upload_path at request time, creates the directory with mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True), and writes each upload under a generated UUID filename.

Market, indicator and AI settings (eodhd_api_key, indicator_service_url, ai_api_endpoint, ai_api_key, ai_api_model) are read inside the corresponding factories rather than at import time, so a misconfigured value surfaces during service resolution or as a stubbed response.

Email delivery is configured from settings (smtp_host, smtp_port, smtp_use_tls, smtp_user, smtp_password, smtp_sender_email) and settings.frontend_url is used to build absolute verification links, price-alert deeplinks and external-account error deeplinks.

Auth security settings are read at call time: totp_max_attempts and totp_lockout_seconds gate the 2FA attempt counter and Redis lockout, and webauthn_rp_id, webauthn_rp_name, webauthn_origin and webauthn_challenge_ttl_seconds configure passkey registration and assertion.
settings.sync_ttl_seconds is applied as the TTL of the Redis set that tracks in-flight account syncs per user.

Settings defines local dev defaults for the whole dev stack (frontend_url, database_url, cors_allow_origins, upload_path, redis_url, indicator_service_url, ai_api_endpoint) so a missing variable degrades to a working single-machine value instead of failing startup, while .env.example supplies the Compose-network values such as the postgres/redis/mailcrab hostnames and http://backend:8000 that take precedence over those defaults.

Registration import style differs: register_services, register_integration_services and register_market_services import their symbols at module scope, while register_integration_stub_services and register_market_stub_services import every symbol lazily inside the function body; that laziness does not keep vendor SDKs out of a stubbed process, because src/config/services.py imports src.integration.registry and src.market at module scope and those import ws_api and eodhd.apiclient respectively, so both SDKs load regardless of STUB_EXTERNAL_API. What the stub modules guarantee is that the implementations are stand-ins: src/stubs/wealthsimple.py and src/stubs/eodhd.py define their own API-client stand-ins instead of importing ws_api or eodhd.apiclient.

register_market_services in src/market/__init__.py registers the same abstract keys as register_market_stub_services with the same factories, with the single exception of AIService (ai_service_factory versus StubAIService); the two functions have no other factory difference.

The market registration list covers the whole domain surface — MarketGateway, DataPlaneMarketGateway, SecurityValuationRepository, ChartSnapshotRepository, SecurityDocumentRepository, SecurityNoteRepository, LogoCache, FxRateProvider, EndpointResponseCache and AlertEvaluationService — and the account domain registers PortfolioRepository plus PortfolioService in src/account/registry.py; a route, service or task that resolves one of these keys fails at request time if its domain's register function is not updated.

src/worker.py and src/main.py are the only production callers of register_services; tests that need a registry build one themselves, and WebSocket request flows construct a container from the registry object rather than from a FastAPI dependency: src/ws/router.py uses svcs.Container(websocket.app.state.svcs_registry) for UserApi and src/worker_dashboard/router.py guards on getattr(websocket.app.state, "svcs_registry", None) before doing the same.

src/core/email.py::EmailService is registered as a value by register_core_services, so every aget(EmailService) — API routes, task bodies and WebSocket paths — returns one shared instance; it renders Jinja templates from src/templates/email/ and sends via aiosmtplib, starting TLS only when settings.smtp_use_tls is set and logging in only when both smtp_user and smtp_password are non-empty, and wrapping any SMTP failure in EmailSendError.

settings.email_verification_token_expiry_hours bounds both the stored token expiry (timedelta(hours=...)) and the itsdangerous max_age (hours * 3600) for email-verification tokens, so the database and serializer deadlines cannot drift apart.

Market and AI settings are read inside factories: eodhd_gateway_factory branches on settings.stub_external_api and reads settings.eodhd_api_key in both branches, indicator_service_client_factory builds a request-scoped httpx client from settings.indicator_service_url and hands it to the svcs container, and ai_service_factory reads settings.ai_api_endpoint, ai_api_key and ai_api_model.

The /health/live probe is an unconditional liveness endpoint returning {"status": "alive"}, while /health/ready resolves an AsyncSession from the svcs container, executes select(1), pings Redis through redis_manager.client(), and returns 200 when both report ok or 503 with status "degraded" otherwise; the Compose backend healthcheck calls /health/live.

Task modules are pinned to the same registry contract: src/integration/task.py joins src/account/task.py and src/market/task.py in raising RuntimeError("Worker registry not initialized") when huey.svcs_registry is None before resolving services inside async with Container(huey.svcs_registry), and tests patch src.account.task.huey.svcs_registry, src.market.task.huey.svcs_registry and src.integration.task.huey.svcs_registry with MagicMock and None.

The tracked .env.example is the sample copied to a gitignored root .env with cp .env.example .env, and the README migration note declares src/.env and frontend/.env obsolete: existing checkouts must move backend overrides and VITE_* overrides into the root .env, delete both files, and add MARKET_DATA_SERVICE_TOKEN.

MARKET_DATA_SERVICE_TOKEN is the shared secret for the MCP gateway to backend data plane: .env.example ships the throwaway dev value dev-market-data-token, docker-compose.yml passes it to the mcp-gateway service together with BACKEND_BASE_URL and DATA_PLANE_PATH (default /api/v1/market/data), and docker-compose.prod.yml asserts it is set with a required-variable expression, so the secret must be rotated on both sides together.

Settings.validate_service_token raises ValueError when MARKET_DATA_SERVICE_TOKEN is empty or whitespace-only and the environment is not dev/test, so a missing service token fails Settings() construction at startup; dev and test are exempt, and tests/test_settings.py covers the prod, staging, whitespace-only, dev and test cases.

Settings.validate_market_provider_keys requires FMP_API_KEY and POLYGON_API_KEY to be non-blank outside dev/test unless stub_external_api is true, raising a ValidationError that names every missing variable and points at STUB_EXTERNAL_API=true as the offline alternative; tests cover both keys missing, FMP-only, Polygon-only, the dev/test exemption, the stub-mode bypass and the valid prod case.

Settings defines seven endpoint-cache TTL fields as the per-data-class lifetimes of the data-plane response cache: endpoint_ttl_prices_seconds 3600, endpoint_ttl_statements_seconds 86400, endpoint_ttl_metrics_seconds 86400, endpoint_ttl_options_seconds 1800, endpoint_ttl_search_seconds 3600, endpoint_ttl_quotes_seconds 30 and endpoint_ttl_negative_seconds 300.

EndpointResponseCache resolves a data class's TTL at cache-write time: _TTL_SETTING_FIELDS maps the data-class string to the Settings attribute and _ttl_for reads it with getattr inside _store, while _negative_ttl reads settings.endpoint_ttl_negative_seconds, so a changed setting value applies to the next write without rebuilding the cache; an unconfigured data class logs a warning and falls back to _DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS = 3600, and an explicit ttl argument overrides the class TTL.

Two svcs keys share the MarketGateway ABC: MarketGateway resolves to eodhd_gateway_factory for legacy price fetch, and DataPlaneMarketGateway — a behaviour-free subclass that exists only as a distinct registration key — resolves to composite_market_gateway_factory for the provider-agnostic data plane; both keys are registered in register_market_services (src/market/__init__.py) and in the stub branch register_market_stub_services (src/config/services.py).

CompositeMarketGateway routes prices, search, symbol lookup, fundamentals and quotes to the FMP gateway and options chains and expirations to the Polygon gateway, and adds no caching of its own because data-plane caching happens one layer above in EndpointResponseCache.

composite_market_gateway_factory is a sync closeable generator factory: it builds both provider gateways, yields the composite, and its finally calls CompositeMarketGateway.close(), which invokes each provider's optional close() hook, so svcs container teardown releases the FMP HTTP client and the Polygon session; it is sync because data_router resolves the key with the sync services.get, and a failed Polygon construction closes the already-built FMP client before re-raising.

lifespan_context resolves DataPlaneMarketGateway eagerly in a throwaway svcs container before serving requests, so a missing provider key or a broken gateway registration fails at boot rather than on the first data-plane request, and each later request-scoped DepContainer builds and closes its own composite.

Stub mode is enforced at both the registry and the factory level for the market domain: eodhd_gateway_factory, fmp_gateway_factory and polygon_gateway_factory each return their Stub*Gateway when settings.stub_external_api is true, so the live registration path still yields an offline composite; the integration domain has no factory-level guard and relies on the registry branch alone.

cors_exception_middleware in src/main.py is a safety net around the FastAPI handlers: on an unhandled exception it returns 500 with CORS headers re-attached for an allowed origin and includes str(exc) in the body outside prod while returning the generic Internal Error in prod.
